newsitem.title: USA: Schwarz Pharma gets FDA letter on EDEX.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma gets FDA letter on EDEX.

text.p: Schwarz Pharma Inc, a unit of German-based Schwarz Pharma AG, said Wednesday it received a U.S. Food and Drug Administration approvable letter for EDEX.

EDEX, or alprostadil for injection, was developed to treat impotence, which affects more than 10 million men in the United States, Schwarz Pharma said. The company said it plans to begin marketing EDEX following final FDA clearance.

Schwarz Pharma said with self-injection of EDEX, 97 percent to 99 percent of patients with erectile dysfunction who chose at-home treatment achieved erections sufficient for intercourse. More than 15,400 self-injections were performed, and more than 90 percent gave satisfactory responses.

Schwarz Pharma said EDEX has an excellent safety profile, determined through clinical trials involving 1,065 patients. The most common side effect was penile pain reported by 31 percent of EDEX patients versus 9 percent of placebo patients.
In guidelines issued earlier this month, Schwarz Pharma said the American Urological Association noted intracavernous injection of alprostadil as a safe and effective treatment for impotence.
